findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed multiple chemical sanitizers to not meet required chemical sanitizing concentrations:
1) The dish machine at the bar (0 ppm Cl). CORRECTED- sanitizer was replaced, machine was primed, and ran until it was observed to be in compliance.
2) The sanitizer bucket was observed at 100 ppm quaternary ammonia. CORRECTED- the bucket was remade to 200 ppm.
Ensure chemical sanitizers used for food contact surfaces are tested at a frequency to ensure the concentration as recommended by the manufacturer's label (50-200 ppm Chlorine, and 200-400 ppm quaternary ammonia).
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A). [P]

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Inspector observed a gallon of milk held past it’s expiration date (6/9/26). CORRECTED- the milk was voluntarily discarded. Ensure prepackaged foods are not held past their expiration or “best by” dates to prevent the growth of pathogens.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(B) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (B) Except as specified in (E) - (G) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and PACKAGED by a FOOD PROCESSING PLANT shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and if the FOOD is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded, based on the temperature and time combinations specified in (A) of this section and: (1) The day the original container is opened in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be counted as Day 1; and (2) The day or date marked by the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT may not exceed a manufacturer’s use-by date if the manufacturer determined the use-by date based on FOOD safety. [Pf]

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment: FIRST REPEAT: Inspector observed the gaskets along the 3 door refrigerator to be frayed. Ensure all nonfood contact surfaces are maintained in proper repair. Correct by next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2. [C]

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the hand washing sink at the bar to only dispense cold water- the hot water faucet was nonoperational. All sinks designated for hand washing should be able to reach a minimum temperature of 85F. Inspector will return on 02/24/25 to check for compliance.
findings.citation_text: 5-202.12(A) Handwashing Sink, Installation. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be equipped to provide water at a temperature of at least 29.4°C (85°F) through a mixing valve or combination faucet. [Pf]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment:

2) 2 ladles handing in ready to use position with an accumulation of food debris on the food contact surfaces. CORRECTED- items were moved to the dish machine for ware washing. 
3) The water fountain in the hallway contains a significant amount of limescale and biofilm.
Ensure all food contact surfaces are maintained clean to sight and touch to prevent the contamination of ready to eat (RTE) foods. Inspector will return on 02/24 to check that line items 1 and 3 have been cleaned.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.  [Pf]

[P]

findings.title: Food properly labeled; original container.
findings.comment:
A blue container with white powder (appeared to be flour) was observed in the dry storage. Discussed with PIC and the labeling of the substance was corrected. Ensure that all items such as white powders that are not easily identifiable are labeled properly.

3-602.11(B)(1)-(4) and (6) Food Labels. (B) Label information shall include: (1) The common name of the FOOD, or absent a common name, an adequately descriptive identity statement; (2) If made from two or more ingredients, a list of ingredients and subingredients in descending order of predominance by weight, including a declaration of artificial colors, artificial flavors and chemical preservatives, if contained in the FOOD; (3) An accurate declaration of the net quantity of contents; (4) The name and place of business of the manufacturer, packer, or distributor; and (6) Except as exempted in the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act § 403(q)(3) - (5), nutrition labeling as specified in 21 CFR 101 - Food Labeling and 9 CFR 317 Subpart B Nutrition Labeling. [C]

3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less. [P]

Facility does not have a probe-style thermometer available for use. CORRECTED- PIC purchased a probe thermometer from GFS during the inspection. Ensure probe-style thermometers are always available in the kitchen for measuring food temperature.
4-302.12: (A) FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be provided and readily accessible for use in ensuring attainment and maintenance of FOOD temperatures. (B) A TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE with a suitable small diameter probe that is designed to measure the temperature of thin masses shall be provided and readily accessible to accurately measure the temperature in thin FOODS such as MEAT patties and FISH filets. [Pf]

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored

3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container (B) In non-TCS FOOD (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form). (D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS (F) In container of water at least 135F and container is properly cleaned. [C]

2-301.14: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands.  [P]

If container or PACKAGE does not bear a date or day or if inappropriately marked with date or day exceeding temperature and time combination. (B) Refrigerated RTE TCS FOOD prepared in FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and dispensed through vending machine shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time. [P]

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.citation_text:
2-103.11 (O) Copies of signed reporting agreements were not available for three of the employees working at the time of inspection. PIC had employees review and sign the reporting agreement during inspection. Ensure all staff are educated on the employee health policy upon hiring and sign reporting agreements prior to beginning their first shift. Maintain signed copies of reporting agreements for staff.
The person in charge shall ensure that food employees are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with law, to the person in charge, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through food, as specified under  2-201.11(A).

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114 Freshly prepared (manually mixed) solutions in sani-buckets at the bar and banquet area had concentrations of 100ppm/below. A very small amount of quat sanitizer was left in the jug used to make the solutions. Steramine tablets were used to remake solutions at 200-400ppm. Ensure test strips are used to verify proper concentration of sanitizer solutions prior to use. 
A quaternary ammonia compound solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. Use test strips to verify concentration.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-602.11 Both soda guns had mold buildup along the surface of the dispenser where nozzle attaches. The inner surface of nozzles also had buildup, especially the soda gun in the banquet area. Ensure frequent cleaning to eliminate buildup. 
Equipment such as beverage dispensing nozzles shall be cleaned at a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11 Table top dicer was stored for use and observed to have soiled food contact surfaces. Stuck on pieces of onion were on the slicing surface and in grooves push block. Equipment was removed to be cleaned and sanitized. Ensure ware washing process, including soaking/pre-cleaning, occurs as many times as needed until all surfaces of equipment are properly cleaned and sanitized. 
Food contact surfaces shall be clean to sight and touch. Properly clean and sanitize food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils between uses.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.citation_text:
3-501.17 Chili, leftover hotdogs, and open gallons of milk were observed without date marks in the walk-in cooler and 3 door cooler. Based on information provided foods were still within 7 day time frame for use. Foods were dated and kept to be used or discarded at the end of 7 days. Ensure prepared foods that require date marking are properly dated and used or discarded w/in 7 days.
Ready to eat time/temperature control for safety foods shall be clearly dated after preparation or after original packaging is opened and shall be used or discarded within 7 days when held under refrigeration. The day of preparation and/or the original packaging is opened shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed
findings.citation_text:
5-403.12 Ponding liquid waste was observed in the base of the soda gun holder at the main bar. Debris buildup appeared to be blocking the drain and inhibiting proper drainage. Ensure cleaning as needed to allow for proper drainage of liquid waste from the soda gun holder.
Condensate drainage and other non-sewage liquids and rainwater shall be drained from point of discharge to disposal according to law.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625  Sec. 3.06 Expired food handler certifications were observed for at least two current employees. PIC noted staff were advised to complete certification and provide updated copies. Ensure all staff that are not certified food managers complete an online food handler certification course within 30 days of hiring, and maintain copies of certifications on-site.
All food handlers, other than someone who has a food manager certification, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:

All certified food managers need to complete the food allergen awareness training by the next routine inspection to ensure a CFM with allergen certification is on-site during all hours of operation.

Solution was mixed by hand to provide a solution at 200-400ppm. A 2oz portion cup was used and marked for reference to prepare sani-bucket solutions. 2-102.11 (A), (B) & (C)(1), (4)-(16) Priority items were observed for handwashing, potential bare hand contact with ready to eat foods, and sanitization. Quat dispenser was not functioning properly, and the pizza cooler was holding at 45F-47F. Active managerial controls were discussed and will be revisited at spot check on 4/22/22. 
Based on the risks inherent to the food operation, during inspections and upon request the PIC shall demonstrate to the regulatory authority knowledge of foodborne disease prevention, application of the hazard analysis and critical control points, and the requirements of the Code.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 Bartender did not wash hands prior to preparing a to go beverage for a customer. Bartender was observed preparing sanitizer solution and doing various general tasks prior to preparing the beverage. Bartender was advised on handwashing between tasks and was later observed washing hands between tasks.  
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles, and after engaging in activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.12 Bartender washed hands without proper technique. Manual faucet was shut off prior to getting paper towels to dry hands. Proper handwashing was discussed. Ensure paper towels are used as a barrier to shut off the manual faucet after drying hands. 
Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink.

findings.title: No bare hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed
findings.citation_text:
3-301.11 Bulk sugar was observed with a mug stored inside, and the handle of the mug was in direct contact with the sugar. Mug was removed for cleaning. Proper storage of scoops to avoid hand contact with ready to eat foods was discussed. 
Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in ¶¶ (D) and (E) of this section, food employees may not contact exposed, ready-to-eat food with their bare hands and shall use suitable utensils such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing equipment.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.citation_text:
3-501.17 1. Leftover baked potatoes and portions of cole slaw in the walk-in cooler and an open bag of mixed greens in the bottom of the sandwich prep cooler were all observed without proper date marks. All items were prepared and opened as of the Saturday prior. Date marks were provided for mixed greens and cole slaw portions. Baked potatoes were prepared for potato skins, portioned and placed in the freezer for storage. 
Ready to eat time/temperature control for safety foods shall be clearly dated after preparation or after original packaging is opened and shall be used or discarded within 7 days when held under refrigeration. The day of preparation and/or the original packaging is opened shall be counted as Day 1.

4-303.11 Prep was underway in the kitchen and sanitizer was not yet prepared. Cook prepared a Quat solution during inspection. Ensure sanitizer solutions are made and are available prior to beginning food prep.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-602.11 1. Soda gun at the bar had mold buildup along the outer edge where the nozzle seals to the gun. The drain cup beneath the soda gun had buildup where the drain hose connected. A small amount of ponding liquid was observed where clog was present. Employee working at the bar was advised the soda gun and drain cup beneath were in need of cleaning.
Equipment such as beverage dispensing nozzles shall be cleaned at a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

2. Mashed potato scoop was soiled with food debris from use during lunch service and stored on top of the lid to the mashed potato container in the hot holding unit. Scoop was cleaned and sanitized in the dish machine during inspection. Ensure cleaning of utensils up to every 4hrs when stored at ambient temperature.
If used with time/temperature control for safety (TCS)foods, equipment food contact surfaces and utensils shall be cleaned throughout the day at least every 4 hours.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 Pan of sloppy joes leftover from the previous operating day had an internal temperature of 46F. Pan was stacked between two other pans of sloppy joes with internal temperatures of 43F-44F. Employee that was in charge of preparing and cooling sloppy joes the day prior stated the products were cooled on ice baths, but the temperature was not monitored during the process. It was unclear as to how long the middle pan of sloppy joes had an internal temperature above 45F, and the product in question was discarded.
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as a public health control, cold TCS foods shall be maintained at 41F/below.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.citation_text:
3-501.18 1. Portions of cole slaw made in-house were observed in a container labeled 11/27 in the walk-in cooler. Remaining portions were discarded during inspection. Ensure foods prepared on-site are used or discarded within 7 days.
2.  Open bag of pepperoni in the bottom of the pizza prep cooler was not date marked. Kitchen staff noted it was opened within the last few days and provided a date mark.
3. Leftover hotdogs in the walk-in cooler were not date marked. Kitchen staff stated they were from service Monday evening. Date mark was provided. 
4. Open bags of shredded lettuce and mixed greens were observed without date marks in the bottom of the prep cooler. Lettuce shreds were opened the day prior, and mixed greens were just opened today. Date marks were provided.
A food specified in ¶ 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in ¶ 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or package that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in ¶ 3501.17(A).

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11 Pizza baking tray was observed with encrusted debris. Staff working at time of inspection noted they had not used the tray in question during current operations. Tray was taken to dish area to be cleaned and sanitized.
The food-contact surfaces of cooking equipment and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.12 1. Hood filters above cooking equipment were soiled with buildup of dust and grease. Hood was last serviced in August 2021 and was due for another full service. Ensure filters are cleaned as needed between full service cleanings.
2. Floor under and around fryers had some buildup of grease and food debris. Floors were cleaned since last inspection but were in need of cleaning again. Ensure the floor under equipment is cleaned as needed to eliminate buildup of grease and food debris.
3. Walls on both sides of the mopsink were damaged along the top edge of base coving. Repair the walls at the mopsink.
Physical facilities shall be maintained in good repair and cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
6-305.11 Jackets were observed hanging on shelving used for storage of clean equipment. Proper storage was discussed, and jackets were removed from the kitchen.
Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be used for the orderly storage of employee clothing and other possessions.
findings.citation_text:
6-303.11 Light bulbs by the back wall in dry storage room were burnt out. Provide adequate lighting in the dry storage room. 
Light intensity shall be at least 10 food candles (108 lux) at a distance of 30 inches above the floor in walk-in refrigeration units and dry storage areas and in other areas and rooms during periods of cleaning.

findings.title: No bare hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed
findings.comment:
3-301.11: Observed the ice scoop stored inside the bar ice container. The handle was inside the ice. Ice surrounding the handle was discarded. The handle was moved out of the ice container. Ensure ice scoop handle is not stored in the ice to minimize contamination from hands. 
(A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall properly wash hands (C). (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall not contact RTE FOODS with bare hands – except washing fruits and veggies (P). (C) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall minimize contact with FOOD that is not RTE (Pf). (D) Contact does not apply to RTE Food being added as ingredient to be cooked. (E) FOOD EMPLOYEES not serving a HSP may contact exposed, RTE with bare hands if approved.

findings.title: Proper cooling time and temperature
findings.comment:
3-501.14: Observed a a container of cheese sauce in the walk in cooler (WIC) to be at a temperature of 90F at approximately 3:45pm. The cheese sauce was made this morning between 10am and 12pm. Ensure foods are properly cooled rapidly. Cheese sauce was discarded during the inspection. 
(A) TCS FOOD shall be cooled within in 2 hours from 135F to 70F. Within 6 hours, FOOD shall cool from 135F to 41F or less. (B) TCS FOOD shall be cooled within 4 hours or less if prepared from ingredients at ambient temperature. (C) TCS FOOD received above 45F in compliance with LAWS shall be cooled within 4 hours. (D) Raw EGGS shall be received and immediately placed in EQUIPMENT with air temperature of 45F or less.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.comment:
3-501.15: Cheese sauce was observed cooling improperly in the walk in cooler. The cheese sauce was cooling inside of a deep contaner and was covered. Ensure foods are rapidly cooled using the methods below. Cheese was discarded during the inspection. 
(A) Cooling shall be accomplished with time and temperature criteria by using following methods: FOOD in shallow pans, Separating FOOD into small portions, using rapid cooling EQUIPMENT, stirring food in container placed in ice bath, containers facilitating heat transfer, adding ice, other effective methods. P (B) When placed in cooling or cold holding EQUIPMENT, FOOD containers shall be: arranged to maximize heat transfer through container walls, loosely covered or uncovered, and during cooling period.
